findings.text: the launch bullet says "Today `_is_own_start` is consulted only in `_resolve_arrival`", but `_feed` consults it a second time (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1755, the start whose arrival hold has already gone), so a node that verifies the premise finds it false

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves at the stated place: `ticker.stream_carries` (:1202), `CARRIED_PANE_WORDS` (:367), `RowPolicy._is_own_start` (:1388), `_resolve_arrival` (:1559), `_release_expired` (:1506), `_observer_exception` (:1521, called from `_feed` at :1827), `transition_class` (:1144), `_display_state`, `PANE_STATES` (:280) and `_watch_transition` (recovery_watch.py:1892); the plan's own anchors `§4`, `§5`, `§7`, `§9` resolve to sections that exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §14's done-when names measurable row sets for three fixtures plus a producer arm calling `recovery_watch._watch_transition`, and each carries a base-revision negative control ("the same sequences at the base revision print none of the launch, the `in review` row, the landing and the dropped row"); the no-repeat arm (`complete → recorded` twice prints one landing) and the flicker/reload arms are additional controls that can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section writes no report or gate log to a scratch path; its only outputs are source files and the new test, and the gate log is the run's own durable evidence.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no ticket, plan-stage or version label reaches a symbol or a comment; `in review` and the extended `CARRIED_PANE_WORDS` rule are named by what they do, and "in review" fits the ten-column `STATE_WORD` half.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the mechanism paragraph's premise that `_is_own_start` is consulted only in `_resolve_arrival` is false at HEAD (the session check is also applied in `_feed` at ticker.py:1755); the rest of the mechanism holds: `stream_carries` does withhold a launch (`_pane_word` of `dispatched → working` is `working`, and `transition_class` returns `ROW_OBSERVER`), `_observer_exception` (ticker.py:1521-1534) does drop a settled row for a run whose delivery was shown (`_told`), `_watch_transition` does write the review run's own `run_id`/`node` (recovery_watch.py:1913-1914) and carries no actor, and the cited measurement reproduces: over the stream window 2026-10-16T19:01Z to 2026-10-23T23:00Z in `~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.events` I count 1,567 `→ recorded` rows across 1,546 runs, 1,439 of them `complete → recorded`, and the maximum for any one run is exactly 6 — within 13 rows (0.8%) of the plan's 1,580 / 1,559 / 1,452, with its "at most six for any one run" exact.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s14 has one deliverable (the stream carries each real state change of a run once); the launch, in-review, landing and dropped rows are arms of that one rule, not separate nodes.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §14's ordering resolves against the live plan: §9 lists `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py` among its wiring node's write paths (plan.html:307) and is `done`, §5 and §7 both write `ticker.py` (plan.html:195, :263), and the open followup `f-alwh-004` recommends §14 first on `ticker.py` and `recovery_watch.py`, matching §14's "after §4, before §5 and §7, and after §9's wiring node".
